The session-cache change is therefore covered at the family level only indirectly (server/client handshakes); the dedicated resumption evidence is the S30 crate test and the focused probe below.

focused_probe.name: s31 TLS1.2 session-id resumption through the candidate DSO
focused_probe.source: court/s31-probe/probe.c (test-only, outside src/ and outside the atlas)
focused_probe.runtime_linkage: ldd probe -> /work/artifacts/phase2/install/lib/libssl.so.3 and libcrypto.so.3 (not the authority)
focused_probe.setup: TLS1.2 max on both sides, SSL_OP_NO_TICKET on both contexts, SSL_SESS_CACHE_SERVER + session id context on a server SSL_CTX that stays alive across two accepts; client uses SSL_get1_session then SSL_set_session
observed_output: RESULT PASS client resumed the TLS1.2 session id
focused_probe.claim: The candidate distribution DSO resumes a TLS1.2 session id with tickets disabled, on both peers; this exercises the S30 session-cache insert/lookup path end-to-end.
focused_probe.limits: One process, loopback, self-signed fixture, no consumer callback re-entrancy and no automatic-flush trigger. It does not substitute for a per-family resumption workload.

non_claims: A passing row is DROP_IN-equivalence at the measured level, not proof of memory safety, constant-time behaviour or complete ABI parity.
The 157 L7 families are bound to libcrypto 2b0ff1b6 / libssl f99f7159; any later install invalidates this binding.
The 11 Phase-2 ABI courts are structural only; every unimplemented symbol is a scaffold that aborts when called.
